title: Compassion fatigue and influencing factors among psychiatric-stationary nurses in Germany: a quantitative cross-sectional study
summary:
In psychiatric care, it is important to show a certain degree of compassion for patients. This gives patients a sense of security and can encourage their willingness to participate in therapy.
People who have a helping profession or who care for other people can develop compassion fatigue. This manifests itself through stress or burnout, which occurs as a result of prolonged work with traumatized people. In general, it can be said that up to 40% of care workers suffer from moderate to severe compassion fatigue.
As no relevant studies from Germany specifically on nurses in psychiatric settings have been found to date and a high level of compassion fatigue in the psychiatric/nursing field has already been demonstrated in other countries, this experience should also be investigated for Germany so that long-term effects on nurses can be prevented. The introduction of suitable measures can reduce compassion fatigue among nurses.
conditions: Survey of compassion fatigue in psychiatric nursing staff

interventions.name: A questionnaire survey of nursing staff in psychiatric inpatient settings in the months of May and June on the subject of compassion fatigue.
